Chapter 1 · Step-by-step

Modern periodic law

Periodic Table & Periodic PropertiesFundamentalsTopic 1 of 30

Explanation

Concept. Modern periodic law (Periodic Table & Periodic Properties, topic 1/30) is a core NEET inorganic idea. Learn the trend or structure first, then the exception and its one-line reason.
Key formula / trend to memorise
Size: down $\uparrow$, across $\downarrow$; IE: $NaAl$; EA: $Cl>F$; EN: $F>O>N$; $Z_{eff}=Z-S$
Make this a flashcard. NEET inorganic MCQs test this trend, colour, structure or test.
Key points.
  • Trend first: size, IE, EA, EN, hydration, lattice, solubility across group and period.
  • Structure: VSEPR shape, hybridisation, MOT bond order, coordination geometry.
  • Colour/magnetism: d-d transitions, charge transfer, spin-only moment.
  • Tests: flame, borax bead, brown ring, precipitates, gases evolved.
  • Exceptions: first-element anomaly, inert pair, lanthanide contraction.
Example 1.

Q. Two species on “Modern periodic law” differ by group or period. Decide the trend.

  1. Write formulae with oxidation states and structures.
  2. Apply size/charge/Fajan/VSEPR/CFT rule as applicable.
  3. Stable or lower-energy option wins; state any exception.

Answer: trend-based option with one-line electronic reason.

Example 2 (NEET pattern).

Q. Identify by colour, precipitate, gas or magnetic moment.

  1. Recall exact observation: flame/bead colour, precipitate, gas smell.
  2. Link to ion or structure; eliminate by formula and charge balance.
  3. Confirm with a second test (AgCl in NH3, BaSO4 insolubility).

Answer: observation gives ion or structure directly.

Common mistakes.
  • Memorising without reason; exceptions then fail.
  • Confusing X-ray structures (XeF4 square planar vs CCl4 tetrahedral).
  • Forgetting charge balance in complexes and salt tests.

Concept. Ionic radius (Periodic Table & Periodic Properties, topic 9/30) is a core NEET inorganic idea. Learn the trend or structure first, then the exception and its one-line reason.
Key formula / trend to memorise
Size: down $\uparrow$, across $\downarrow$; IE: $NaAl$; EA: $Cl>F$; EN: $F>O>N$; $Z_{eff}=Z-S$
Make this a flashcard. NEET inorganic MCQs test this trend, colour, structure or test.
Key points.
  • Trend first: size, IE, EA, EN, hydration, lattice, solubility across group and period.
  • Structure: VSEPR shape, hybridisation, MOT bond order, coordination geometry.
  • Colour/magnetism: d-d transitions, charge transfer, spin-only moment.
  • Tests: flame, borax bead, brown ring, precipitates, gases evolved.
  • Exceptions: first-element anomaly, inert pair, lanthanide contraction.
Example 1.

Q. Two species on “Ionic radius” differ by group or period. Decide the trend.

  1. Write formulae with oxidation states and structures.
  2. Apply size/charge/Fajan/VSEPR/CFT rule as applicable.
  3. Stable or lower-energy option wins; state any exception.

Answer: trend-based option with one-line electronic reason.

Example 2 (NEET pattern).

Q. Identify by colour, precipitate, gas or magnetic moment.

  1. Recall exact observation: flame/bead colour, precipitate, gas smell.
  2. Link to ion or structure; eliminate by formula and charge balance.
  3. Confirm with a second test (AgCl in NH3, BaSO4 insolubility).

Answer: observation gives ion or structure directly.

Common mistakes.
  • Memorising without reason; exceptions then fail.
  • Confusing X-ray structures (XeF4 square planar vs CCl4 tetrahedral).
  • Forgetting charge balance in complexes and salt tests.

Concept. Effective nuclear charge (Periodic Table & Periodic Properties, topic 24/30) is a core NEET inorganic idea. Learn the trend or structure first, then the exception and its one-line reason.
Key formula / trend to memorise
Size: down $\uparrow$, across $\downarrow$; IE: $NaAl$; EA: $Cl>F$; EN: $F>O>N$; $Z_{eff}=Z-S$
Make this a flashcard. NEET inorganic MCQs test this trend, colour, structure or test.
Key points.
  • Trend first: size, IE, EA, EN, hydration, lattice, solubility across group and period.
  • Structure: VSEPR shape, hybridisation, MOT bond order, coordination geometry.
  • Colour/magnetism: d-d transitions, charge transfer, spin-only moment.
  • Tests: flame, borax bead, brown ring, precipitates, gases evolved.
  • Exceptions: first-element anomaly, inert pair, lanthanide contraction.
Example 1.

Q. Two species on “Effective nuclear charge” differ by group or period. Decide the trend.

  1. Write formulae with oxidation states and structures.
  2. Apply size/charge/Fajan/VSEPR/CFT rule as applicable.
  3. Stable or lower-energy option wins; state any exception.

Answer: trend-based option with one-line electronic reason.

Example 2 (NEET pattern).

Q. Identify by colour, precipitate, gas or magnetic moment.

  1. Recall exact observation: flame/bead colour, precipitate, gas smell.
  2. Link to ion or structure; eliminate by formula and charge balance.
  3. Confirm with a second test (AgCl in NH3, BaSO4 insolubility).

Answer: observation gives ion or structure directly.

Common mistakes.
  • Memorising without reason; exceptions then fail.
  • Confusing X-ray structures (XeF4 square planar vs CCl4 tetrahedral).
  • Forgetting charge balance in complexes and salt tests.

Key points.

  • Tests: flame, borax bead, brown ring, precipitates, gases evolved.
  • Exceptions: first-element anomaly, inert pair, lanthanide contraction.
Example 1.

Q. Two species on “Hydrogen bonding” differ by group or period. Decide the trend.

  1. Write formulae with oxidation states and structures.

  3. Stable or lower-energy option wins; state any exception.

Example 2 (NEET pattern).

Explanation

Key formula / trend to memorise
Size: down $\uparrow$, across $\downarrow$; IE: $NaAl$; EA: $Cl>F$; EN: $F>O>N$; $Z_{eff}=Z-S$

Key points.
  • Trend first: size, IE, EA, EN, hydration, lattice, solubility across group and period.
  • Structure: VSEPR shape, hybridisation, MOT bond order, coordination geometry.
  • Colour/magnetism: d-d transitions, charge transfer, spin-only moment.
  • Tests: flame, borax bead, brown ring, precipitates, gases evolved.
  • Exceptions: first-element anomaly, inert pair, lanthanide contraction.
Example 1.

Q. Two species on “Oxidation states” differ by group or period. Decide the trend.

Concept. NO (Group 15 - Nitrogen Family, topic 18/35) is a core NEET inorganic idea. Learn the trend or structure first, then the exception and its one-line reason.
Key formula / trend to memorise
$NH_3$ pyramidal; brown ring $[Fe(H_2O)_5NO]^{2+}$; $H_3PO_2$ monobasic, $H_3PO_3$ dibasic
Make this a flashcard. NEET inorganic MCQs test this trend, colour, structure or test.
Key points.
  • Trend first: size, IE, EA, EN, hydration, lattice, solubility across group and period.
  • Structure: VSEPR shape, hybridisation, MOT bond order, coordination geometry.
  • Colour/magnetism: d-d transitions, charge transfer, spin-only moment.
  • Tests: flame, borax bead, brown ring, precipitates, gases evolved.
  • Exceptions: first-element anomaly, inert pair, lanthanide contraction.
Example 1.

Q. Two species on “NO” differ by group or period. Decide the trend.

  1. Write formulae with oxidation states and structures.
  2. Apply size/charge/Fajan/VSEPR/CFT rule as applicable.
  3. Stable or lower-energy option wins; state any exception.

Answer: trend-based option with one-line electronic reason.

Example 2 (NEET pattern).

Q. Identify by colour, precipitate, gas or magnetic moment.

  1. Recall exact observation: flame/bead colour, precipitate, gas smell.
  2. Link to ion or structure; eliminate by formula and charge balance.
  3. Confirm with a second test (AgCl in NH3, BaSO4 insolubility).

Answer: observation gives ion or structure directly.

Common mistakes.
  • Memorising without reason; exceptions then fail.
  • Confusing X-ray structures (XeF4 square planar vs CCl4 tetrahedral).
  • Forgetting charge balance in complexes and salt tests.

d- and f-Block Elementsd-f & CoordinationTopic 22 of 34

Explanation

Concept. Oxidation states of actinides (d- and f-Block Elements, topic 22/34) is a core NEET inorganic idea. Learn the trend or structure first, then the exception and its one-line reason.
Key formula / trend to memorise
Size: down $\uparrow$, across $\downarrow$; IE: $NaAl$; EA: $Cl>F$; EN: $F>O>N$; $Z_{eff}=Z-S$
Make this a flashcard. NEET inorganic MCQs test this trend, colour, structure or test.
Key points.
  • Trend first: size, IE, EA, EN, hydration, lattice, solubility across group and period.
  • Structure: VSEPR shape, hybridisation, MOT bond order, coordination geometry.
  • Colour/magnetism: d-d transitions, charge transfer, spin-only moment.
  • Tests: flame, borax bead, brown ring, precipitates, gases evolved.
  • Exceptions: first-element anomaly, inert pair, lanthanide contraction.
Example 1.

Q. Two species on “Oxidation states of actinides” differ by group or period. Decide the trend.

  1. Write formulae with oxidation states and structures.
  2. Apply size/charge/Fajan/VSEPR/CFT rule as applicable.
  3. Stable or lower-energy option wins; state any exception.

Answer: trend-based option with one-line electronic reason.

Example 2 (NEET pattern).

Q. Identify by colour, precipitate, gas or magnetic moment.

  1. Recall exact observation: flame/bead colour, precipitate, gas smell.
  2. Link to ion or structure; eliminate by formula and charge balance.
  3. Confirm with a second test (AgCl in NH3, BaSO4 insolubility).

Answer: observation gives ion or structure directly.

Common mistakes.
  • Memorising without reason; exceptions then fail.
  • Confusing X-ray structures (XeF4 square planar vs CCl4 tetrahedral).
  • Forgetting charge balance in complexes and salt tests.

Concept. Crystal field theory (Coordination Compounds, topic 31/45) is a core NEET inorganic idea. Learn the trend or structure first, then the exception and its one-line reason.
Key formula / trend to memorise
EAN $=Z-ox+2\times CN$; $\Delta_o$: $t_{2g}$ vs $e_g$; strong: $CN^->NO_2^->en>NH_3>H_2O>F^-$
Make this a flashcard. NEET inorganic MCQs test this trend, colour, structure or test.
Key points.
  • Trend first: size, IE, EA, EN, hydration, lattice, solubility across group and period.
  • Structure: VSEPR shape, hybridisation, MOT bond order, coordination geometry.
  • Colour/magnetism: d-d transitions, charge transfer, spin-only moment.
  • Tests: flame, borax bead, brown ring, precipitates, gases evolved.
  • Exceptions: first-element anomaly, inert pair, lanthanide contraction.
Example 1.

Q. Two species on “Crystal field theory” differ by group or period. Decide the trend.

  1. Write formulae with oxidation states and structures.
  2. Apply size/charge/Fajan/VSEPR/CFT rule as applicable.
  3. Stable or lower-energy option wins; state any exception.

Answer: trend-based option with one-line electronic reason.

Example 2 (NEET pattern).

Q. Identify by colour, precipitate, gas or magnetic moment.

  1. Recall exact observation: flame/bead colour, precipitate, gas smell.
  2. Link to ion or structure; eliminate by formula and charge balance.
  3. Confirm with a second test (AgCl in NH3, BaSO4 insolubility).

Answer: observation gives ion or structure directly.

Common mistakes.
  • Memorising without reason; exceptions then fail.
  • Confusing X-ray structures (XeF4 square planar vs CCl4 tetrahedral).
  • Forgetting charge balance in complexes and salt tests.

Chapter 14 · Step-by-step

Minerals and ores

Metallurgy / General Principles of ExtractionAppliedTopic 1 of 32

Explanation

Concept. Minerals and ores (Metallurgy / General Principles of Extraction, topic 1/32) is a core NEET inorganic idea. Learn the trend or structure first, then the exception and its one-line reason.
Key formula / trend to memorise
Ellingham: lower $\Delta G$ line reduces higher; $\Delta G^\circ=-RT\ln K$
Make this a flashcard. NEET inorganic MCQs test this trend, colour, structure or test.
Key points.
  • Trend first: size, IE, EA, EN, hydration, lattice, solubility across group and period.
  • Structure: VSEPR shape, hybridisation, MOT bond order, coordination geometry.
  • Colour/magnetism: d-d transitions, charge transfer, spin-only moment.
  • Tests: flame, borax bead, brown ring, precipitates, gases evolved.
  • Exceptions: first-element anomaly, inert pair, lanthanide contraction.
Example 1.

Q. Two species on “Minerals and ores” differ by group or period. Decide the trend.

  1. Write formulae with oxidation states and structures.
  2. Apply size/charge/Fajan/VSEPR/CFT rule as applicable.
  3. Stable or lower-energy option wins; state any exception.

Answer: trend-based option with one-line electronic reason.

Example 2 (NEET pattern).

Q. Identify by colour, precipitate, gas or magnetic moment.

  1. Recall exact observation: flame/bead colour, precipitate, gas smell.
  2. Link to ion or structure; eliminate by formula and charge balance.
  3. Confirm with a second test (AgCl in NH3, BaSO4 insolubility).

Answer: observation gives ion or structure directly.

Common mistakes.
  • Memorising without reason; exceptions then fail.
  • Confusing X-ray structures (XeF4 square planar vs CCl4 tetrahedral).
  • Forgetting charge balance in complexes and salt tests.

  • Memorising without reason; exceptions then fail.
  • Confusing X-ray structures (XeF4 square planar vs CCl4 tetrahedral).
  • Forgetting charge balance in complexes and salt tests.

Multiple-correct inorganic problems

Inorganic Exceptions, Trends & Advanced Master ChapterMasteryTopic 19 of 20

Explanation

Concept. Multiple-correct inorganic problems (Inorganic Exceptions, Trends & Advanced Master Chapter, topic 19/20) is a core NEET inorganic idea. Learn the trend or structure first, then the exception and its one-line reason.
Key formula / trend to memorise
Trends beat memory: compare size, charge, $Z_{eff}$ and $\Delta G$; note the exception
Make this a flashcard. NEET inorganic MCQs test this trend, colour, structure or test.
Key points.
  • Trend first: size, IE, EA, EN, hydration, lattice, solubility across group and period.
  • Structure: VSEPR shape, hybridisation, MOT bond order, coordination geometry.
  • Colour/magnetism: d-d transitions, charge transfer, spin-only moment.
  • Tests: flame, borax bead, brown ring, precipitates, gases evolved.
  • Exceptions: first-element anomaly, inert pair, lanthanide contraction.
Example 1.

Q. Two species on “Multiple-correct inorganic problems” differ by group or period. Decide the trend.

  1. Write formulae with oxidation states and structures.
  2. Apply size/charge/Fajan/VSEPR/CFT rule as applicable.
  3. Stable or lower-energy option wins; state any exception.

Answer: trend-based option with one-line electronic reason.

Example 2 (NEET pattern).

Q. Identify by colour, precipitate, gas or magnetic moment.

  1. Recall exact observation: flame/bead colour, precipitate, gas smell.
  2. Link to ion or structure; eliminate by formula and charge balance.
  3. Confirm with a second test (AgCl in NH3, BaSO4 insolubility).

Answer: observation gives ion or structure directly.

Common mistakes.
  • Memorising without reason; exceptions then fail.
  • Confusing X-ray structures (XeF4 square planar vs CCl4 tetrahedral).
  • Forgetting charge balance in complexes and salt tests.
